## ⚠ LESSON: the agent chat is a full, visible conversation — NEVER a one-line input
The user↔agent interaction is messy, multi-turn, back-and-forth, and often NOT cleanly
summarizable. ALWAYS show the ENTIRE chat history as a real scrollable conversation (the
dock), with the settled "Current setup" plan PINNED at the top as the artifact. Do NOT

changelog. The pinned plan is the source of truth for what will slice; the thread below it
is disposable exploration that stays fully visible. (Decided turns 3–4; regressed in turn 6.

## Core conceptual model
- One app = a slicer. Home shows TWO concepts: **Projects** (your work; opens the Prepare
  screen) and **Printers** (your equipment: connection, model, filament/AMS colours,
  calibration, and a **Launch monitor** button). The monitor is a sub-window launched from a
  printer — never a co-equal app.
- Navigation = model **A**: one main window that navigates Home ⇄ Prepare/Check (+ Info) ⇄
  Printer config. Only monitor windows pop out (one per printer, many at once). Opening a
  second project REPLACES the first in the main window; you switch projects via Home. The
  ORCA logo / back control top-left returns to Home; projects auto-save.
- Ownership boundary: the USER supplies what is physically true, what the geometry MEANS, and
  the desired OUTCOME, and holds authority over consequential physical actions. The AGENT owns
  the ~247 invisible process settings (layers, walls, infill, speed, cooling, supports, seams…).
- Printer/filament/colour/model are FACTS ABOUT THE MACHINE → they live in Printer config. The
  project just POINTS at a printer via a loose picker (default: last-used / whatever's idle;
  changeable anytime, never a required first step). Colour INVENTORY = printer; colour→region
  MAPPING = project.
- Painting = annotate MEANING ("smooth face", "bearing surface", "screw hole", "no supports
  here"), and the agent DERIVES the modifiers — not user-set local wall counts / speeds.
- App-level presets/profiles/materials SHIP with the app; most users never touch them. They are
  discoverable only behind the "see all" door, when presets aren't enough. Do not give them
  prime real estate (fold into Preferences).

## Prepare-screen design principles
1. The agent is a SECOND input path, so every visible tool is an OPTIONAL accelerator — anything
   a tool does, you can also just ask for. Beginners talk; makers grab the tool.
2. The conversation is ALWAYS visible (see the lesson above): full history + pinned plan.
3. Four fixed zones, learned once: machine (top) · object on the plate (centre) · intent+plan

4. Words/outcomes on the surface; numbers/parameters one "see all" layer down.
5. Depth opens as a dismissible layer over/beside the current context; the standing screen never
   permanently accumulates.

- **Project window** (one main window, model A) with modes: **Prepare** (plate + tools + dock),

  knowledge: author, licence, safety, BOM, assembly, pictures, versions).
- **Printer config** — sections: Setup · Filament/AMS · Calibration · Maintenance & Privacy.
- **Monitor window** — pop-out per printer: camera, progress, temps, Pause/Resume/Stop, alerts.
- **Dialogs / overlays**: Send (preflight, one-way), the "see all" expert-settings layer,
  Preferences (app-level: cloud, offline, network, updates, presets/materials library).

1	# Spike: identifying a printer from what someone types
2	
3	Prototype for replacing `printer_catalog_search` — the keyword filter in
4	`OrcaPrinterBackend::search_catalog` that requires every word of the query to
5	appear in a printer's name — with the whole catalogue in the model's prompt.
6	
7	The question this spike answers: **if you hand the model all 383 packaged
8	printer models and let it do the interpreting, how often does it get the right
9	printer?**
10	
11	Words only. Photos are the next spike.
12	
13	## Layout
14	
15	| file | what it is |
16	| --- | --- |
17	| `build_catalog.py` | reads `resources/profiles/` and dumps one entry per model |
18	| `catalog.json` | 383 models: id, vendor, model, build volume, nozzles, material |
19	| `catalog.txt` | the compact form that goes in the prompt (~3,700 tokens) |
20	| `instructions.txt` | prompt v1 |
21	| `instructions.v2.txt` | prompt v2 — adds the prefix-ambiguity rule |
22	| `corpus.jsonl` | 50 test cases with expected outcomes |
23	| `schema.json` | JSON shape the model must answer in |
24	| `run.sh` | chat with the assistant yourself, or `--batch` to run the corpus |
25	| `turn.py` | chat-mode helper: builds each turn's case, prints the answer, keeps the history |
26	| `score.py` | scores a run against the corpus |
27	| `compare.py` | shows where repeat runs disagree |
28	| `instructions.v2r2.txt`, `instructions.v2r3.txt` | byte-identical copies of v2; the run is named after the instruction file, so repeats need their own copy |
29	| `out/<run>/` | per-case prompt, raw answer and log |
30	
31	## Trying it yourself
32	
33	```bash
34	./run.sh
35	```
36	
37	Type what printer you have, the way a person would. Each answer shows what the
38	assistant said, the cards it would draw (with build volume and catalog id), and
39	whether it asked a question or called the printer unsupported. The conversation
40	carries across turns, so you can correct it ("no wait, the S1") or answer its
41	question ("the small one").
42	
43	- `/photo PATH [words]` attaches a photo (the path may contain spaces); the
44	  chat uses the photo-aware prompt from `../printer-photos/` by default
45	- `/reset` starts a new conversation
46	- `/raw` toggles the model's raw JSON answer
47	- `/quit` leaves
48	- `-m <model>` and `-i <instructions file>` pick another model or prompt
49	  (default `gpt-5.6-terra` and `instructions.v2.txt`)
50	
51	Every turn's full prompt and answer are kept in the temp folder printed at
52	start, for when you want to see exactly what the model was given. A card marked
53	`INVENTED ID` means the model named a printer that is not in the catalogue.
54	
55	## Running the corpus
56	
57	```bash
58	./run.sh --batch -j 8
59	./score.py gpt-5.6-terra-v2
60	```
61	
62	`--batch` skips cases that already have a result, so delete `out/<run>/` to
63	redo one. The run is named after the model and the instructions file.
64	
65	If the profiles change, rebuild the catalogue first:
66	
67	```bash
68	./build_catalog.py ../../../../resources/profiles > catalog.json && python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('catalog.json'));open('catalog.txt','w').write(chr(10).join(f\"{e['catalogId']} | {e['buildVolume'] or '?'}\" for e in d))"
69	```
70	
71	## The corpus
72	
73	50 cases in nine shapes:
74	
75	- **name-in-sentence** (9) — the real model name inside ordinary speech
76	- **ambiguous-partial** (8) — "bambu a1", where several models fit
77	- **clue-only** (7) — "the ender with the touchscreen", no model name at all
78	- **size-only** (6) — a bed size and nothing else
79	- **not-in-catalogue** (6) — resin printers, laser cutters, models we don't ship
80	- **typo** (6) — "ender3v2", "neptun 4 pro", "BAMBU LAB A1 MINI"
81	- **correction** (4) — a second turn that revises the first
82	- **non-english** (2) — Spanish and Chinese, including the Chinese brand name
83	- **junk** (2) — gibberish, and a question that isn't an identification
84	
85	Each case declares the ids that must appear, the ids that may appear, a card
86	cap, and whether a question is required. Scoring is automatic except for the
87	prose, which needs reading.
88	
89	The scorer's hardest check is **invented ids**: any catalogId not in
90	`catalog.json` is a fail, because it means a card that cannot be installed.
91	
92	## Results (2026-09-17, gpt-5.6-terra via the `codex` CLI)
93	
94	**Prompt v1 — 47/50.** Three failures, all the same mistake: when the query
95	exactly equals one model name but is also the start of others, it showed that
96	one model alone. "bambu a1" got the A1 without the A1 mini; "bambu x1" got the
97	X1 without the X1 Carbon; "ender 3" got the bare Ender-3 out of twelve.
98	
99	**Prompt v2 — 50/50 on the first run.** v2 adds one rule: a query that starts
100	more than one model name is not a clear match even when it exactly equals one
101	of them. That rule alone fixed all three.
102	
103	**Repeats of v2 partly blocked.** The Codex account hit its usage limit after
104	129 calls, so runs 2 and 3 completed only 15 and 14 of the 50 cases.
105	
106	**Pooled across the three v2 runs — 78 passes, 1 failure in 79 case-runs.**
107	The one failure is "bambu x1" in run 3, which reverted to the v1 behaviour and
108	showed the X1 alone.
109	
110	Of the 14 cases that completed in all three v2 runs, 11 gave identical answers.
111	All three that varied were partial-name cases (`prusa mini`, `ender 3`,
112	`bambu x1`). Two of the three varied harmlessly — the same cards, labelled
113	`ask` in one run and `propose` in another. One varied into a wrong answer.
114	
115	**No invented catalog ids in any run.** That was the failure mode most worth
116	measuring and it did not occur once in 129 calls.
117	
118	**A corpus bug the model caught.** Case E07 expected "snapmaker artisan" to be
119	unsupported. The Snapmaker Artisan is in fact packaged. The model was right and
120	the corpus was wrong; E07 is now a positive case.
121	
122	**These runs used a catalogue with gaps.** The first version of
123	`build_catalog.py` did not follow the `inherits` chain in machine presets, so
124	63 of the 383 models went into the prompt with build volume `?` — the Bambu
125	Lab A1 and the Snapmaker Artisan among them. The app itself resolves
126	inheritance (`PrinterCatalog.cpp`, `resolve_machine`). The dump now does too,
127	leaving 9 unknown. Every result above was recorded with the gappy catalogue, so
128	the size-based cases were tested with less information than the app has. They
129	should be re-run.
130	
131	### What the numbers do not cover
132	
133	- Only one model was tested, on one day.
134	- Repeats cover 14 of 50 cases, weighted toward the first two shapes.
135	- Automatic scoring judges which cards were shown and whether a question was
136	  asked. It does not judge the prose; that was read by hand once.
137	- The catalogue here keys on `<vendor folder>/<model name>`, while
138	  `OrcaPrinterBackend` keys on `<vendor id>/<model id>`. Same one-per-model
139	  granularity, different spelling.
140	- 383 models are dumped here; the app counts 384. One model has no machine
141	  preset naming it, so this dump drops it.
142	- 9 models still have no build volume after resolving inheritance (six are
143	  Creality `_CFS-C` duplicates). Not chased.

# Spike: identifying a printer from a photo

Second half of the printer-identification spike. The first half,
`../printer-naming/`, tested words; this one tests photos, alone and together
with a few words. Same approach: the whole packaged catalogue is in the prompt
and the model does the identifying.

## Layout

| file | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| `corpus.jsonl` | 15 cases: 12 photos alone, 3 photos with words |
| `instructions.txt` | photo prompt v1: the words prompt v2 plus a section on reading photos |
| `instructions.v2.txt` | photo prompt v2: adds rules on printed sizes, shape-only guesses and clones |
| `schema.json` | answer shape; adds `evidence`, what the model says it saw |
| `run.sh` | runs the corpus; `-i` picks the prompt, `-t` tags the run |
| `score.py` | scores one or more runs |
| `out/<run>/` | per case: the photo as attached, the prompt, the answer, the log |

The photos are **not** in the repo. They live in `~/Downloads/printer-photos/`
with `ground-truth.json` (source page, author, licence, expected answer). They
are Wikimedia Commons photos under CC0, CC BY and CC BY-SA; the CC BY ones need
credit if they are ever published. `out/` holds copies, and `.gitignore` keeps
them out.

**The model can read an attachment's filename.** Codex sends each image with
its path as text, `<image name=[Image #1] path="...">`, using the path exactly
as passed on the command line; attached as `zebra-canary-7731.jpg` and asked,
the model quoted the name back. So each photo is copied under a random name
(`6d768f52812d.jpg`) and attached by that bare name from inside its folder: no
filename such as "Problemen met neptune 4 Max Elegoo.jpg", no run tag and no
case number reaches the model. `out/<run>/<case>.attached` records which random
name a case used. The chat in `../printer-naming/` does the same.

The photos' embedded metadata was checked with exiftool: none carries a title,
description or keyword naming the printer.

The first runs attached photos as `out/<run>/P09.jpg`; the spike was then
rerun with random names. Both sets are below.

./run.sh -i instructions.v2.txt -t mine

Removed the invented "community profile" framing.** I had written a code comment calling Orca Arena's bundle "community-tuned" and an agent instruction telling the model to prefer "the manufacturer's profile before a community or clone profile." Added the test you asked for.** [tests/jusprin/test_printer_catalog.cpp](tests/jusprin/test_printer_catalog.cpp) loads the real packaged profiles (not a fixture) and checks two things: the vendor id actually exists in the raw catalogue data (proving the constant isn't a typo, and proving the underlying data OrcaSlicer's own wizard would read is untouched), and that filtering by it actually removes something. input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Identify printers from the whole catalog, not a keyword search

The agent used to search a keyword filter that dropped real matches
("voron 2.4 350mm" found nothing) and, when a query exactly matched a
model name that also prefixed others, treated a wrong single match as
certain -- "x1c" resolved to Orca Arena's X1 Carbon with confidence.

Replace printer_catalog_search and printer_propose with one tool,
printer_identify, driven by the whole packaged catalogue (~384 models)
in the session's own instructions, adopting the prefix-ambiguity rule
and photo-evidence rules a naming/photo spike validated separately.
Every catalogId it answers with is checked against the real catalogue;
an unknown one is a tool error the model can correct itself, not an
invented printer.

Orca Arena's undocumented second X1 Carbon bundle is now hidden from
this flow specifically (the agent's catalogue and, later, the in-panel
browse list) by one named vendor-id constant, never by editing the
OrcaSlicer-owned profile files; OrcaSlicer's own wizard and preset
lists are unaffected. Verified against the real packaged profiles in
tests/jusprin/test_printer_catalog.cpp, and live in the built app
against all of the handoff's identification cases.
EOF
)"
